content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Write equations for reactions between acids and carbonates
Describe and test for the gas produced
Use carbonate reactions to prepare salts
Carbonates and hydrogen carbonates react with acids to produce a salt, water, and
. The fizzing produced makes these reactions easy to identify.
Note: Hydrogen carbonates produce the same products but with different ratios.
Bubble the gas through limewater (calcium hydroxide solution)
[DIAGRAM: Delivery tube from reaction flask bubbling gas into test tube of limewater, which turns cloudy]
The white calcium carbonate precipitate causes the milky appearance.
Fizzing/effervescence, solid dissolves, gas turns limewater milky
Green solid dissolves, fizzing, solution turns blue, limewater goes cloudy
Solid dissolves, vigorous fizzing, limewater goes cloudy
Some indigestion tablets contain calcium carbonate
Baking soda (NaHCO₃) reacts with acids in recipes
Acid rain attacks limestone buildings and statues
CaCO₃ + acid rain → dissolves over time
Write the equation for the reaction of calcium carbonate with dilute nitric acid. Include state symbols.
Describe what you would see when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to green copper carbonate powder.
The solution turns blue (copper chloride solution)
The gas produced turns limewater milky/cloudy
Describe the test for carbon dioxide gas and give the result.
Bubble the gas through limewater (calcium hydroxide solution)
If carbon dioxide is present, the limewater turns milky/cloudy/white
This is because calcium carbonate precipitate forms
Explain why calcium carbonate can be used as an antacid.
Calcium carbonate is a base (it can neutralise acids)
The carbonate neutralises the excess stomach acid
This relieves the symptoms of indigestion
The products (calcium chloride, water, CO₂) are harmless
Forgetting that THREE products are formed
Confusing the test for CO₂ with the test for H₂
CO₂ → limewater goes milky; H₂ → squeaky pop
Writing the wrong formula for carbonates
Carbonate ion is CO₃²⁻, hydrogen carbonate is HCO₃⁻
Write the general word equation for the reaction of a carbonate with an acid. (1 mark)
a) Calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid (2 marks)
b) Sodium carbonate + sulfuric acid (2 marks)
c) Copper carbonate + nitric acid (2 marks)
Describe the test for carbon dioxide and state what you would observe. (2 marks)
A student adds dilute hydrochloric acid to copper carbonate.
a) Write the equation for the reaction. (2 marks)
b) Describe what the student would observe. (3 marks)
Write the ionic equation showing what happens to carbonate ions in acid. (2 marks)
Explain why limestone buildings are damaged by acid rain. (3 marks)
